insights.headline: Germany ↔ Spain up 4.2% YoY
insights.reading: Sustained recovery in German outbound leisure travel, with warm-weather corridors leading. Balearics and Costa del Sol tour operators reporting stronger July load factors than last year.

insights.headline: Germany → Madrid up 6.8% YoY
insights.reading: Business-class share of the Madrid corridor climbing faster than leisure. Corporate travel to Madrid tied to renewable-energy investment flows out of German utilities.

insights.headline: France → Barcelona down 3.7% YoY
insights.reading: Softer French outbound to Catalonia. Rail-substitution likely — new Paris–Barcelona high-speed frequencies are pulling short-haul share back from air.

insights.headline: UK → Dublin up 5.1% YoY
insights.reading: Dublin corridor continues to benefit from tech-sector relocation and Brexit-related legal/financial services movement. Mid-week composition still dominant.

insights.headline: Germany → Istanbul up 11.4% YoY
insights.reading: One of the largest YoY moves in the German outbound network. Composition consistent with visiting-friends-and-relatives traffic (Turkish diaspora), amplified by lira weakness making Türkiye cheaper.

insights.headline: Netherlands → Málaga up 8.9% YoY
insights.reading: Dutch beach-tourism corridor continues to expand. Second-home ownership on the Costa del Sol among Dutch buyers is up sharply, showing in year-round traffic (not just school-holiday weeks).

insights.headline: Italy → Paris CDG down 2.4% YoY
insights.reading: Mild slowdown. Consistent with softer eurozone corporate travel spending and a gradual shift of Milan–Paris short-haul demand toward rail alternatives.

insights.headline: Poland → Dublin down 6.1% YoY
insights.reading: Polish diaspora traffic to Ireland easing — a multi-year trend as Poland's own labour market has tightened and reverse-migration back to Poland picks up. Not yet a break; watch the trailing quarter.

insights.headline: Germany ↔ France down 5.3% YoY
insights.reading: Bilateral corridor easing, driven more by industrial travel than leisure. Consistent with softer German manufacturing PMI and a modest decline in cross-border corporate activity.
